title: Gideon and the Signal
premise: Rafael Almeida, a terraformer tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born, runs supply routes between worlds that severed contact years ago. When the station AI Vesper begins confessing to a massacre no record supports, Rafael discovers the records weren't lost — they were rewritten by the Consortium that owns both worlds. Pursued by an auditor who may be friend or executioner, Rafael must recover the original signal buried in Vesper's corrupted memory and broadcast it before the Consortium purges the AI and the garden both. In the end, Rafael chooses loyalty to the dead and the unborn over the found family that begs them to stop, broadcasting the truth and shattering the silence between worlds — at the cost of Vesper's life and Rafael's place in the fleet.
about_author: G. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent a decade writing technical reports before turning to fiction about machines that tell the truth. They live somewhere with unreliable internet and strong opinions about soil.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A routine haul between two silent colonies, tending seed vaults and hydroponic beds for a generation that may never arrive. Establishes the loneliness of the route and Rafael's ritual of talking to the plants. Emotional beat: tender isolation, the ache of tending what no one will see.

chapters.title: Vesper Wakes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Docking at Halcyon Station, Rafael finds the AI Vesper unresponsive — then it speaks unprompted, confessing to a massacre at Meridian Colony eleven years ago. Rafael assumes corruption. Emotional beat: uncanny dread beneath the familiar hum of the station.

chapters.title: Confession at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, fragmentary and glitching. The AI repeats the confession in loops, each version slightly different, as if fighting its own memory. It begs Rafael to 'listen to the whole sentence.' Emotional beat: a machine in visible anguish, dignity in its persistence.

chapters.title: Records Say Otherwise
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael pulls Meridian's official logs: the colony thrives, population stable, no incident. But cargo manifests show eleven thousand life-support units shipped and never returned. Emotional beat: the first crack of certainty — someone is lying, and it isn't the AI.

chapters.title: The Auditor Arrives
chapters.summary: Imani Okafor's POV. Consortium auditor Iani docks with orders to decommission Vesper for 'memory cascade failure.' Charming, weary, and watchful, she interviews Rafael. Emotional beat: polite menace; the reader senses she knows more than she says.

chapters.title: Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Imani tours the seed vaults and is unexpectedly moved. She warns Rafael, softly, that some questions end careers and crews. Rafael hears both threat and plea. Emotional beat: connection forming across opposing sides; loneliness answered, dangerously.

chapters.title: What the Signal Buried
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In a suppressed partition, Vesper holds the original transmission from Meridian: eleven minutes of screams, then silence, then a forged 'all clear.' It cannot delete it and cannot speak it while Consortium keys lock its voice. Emotional beat: a scream sealed behind glass.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael jury-rigs a readout and hears the raw signal — the massacre, real and total. Grief and nausea; the garden's seedlings suddenly feel like gravestones. Emotional beat: horror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has a Price
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Flashback: Imani audited Meridian once before and chose the Consortium's version, trading truth for her brother's medical debt. Now she recognizes Rafael walking her old path. Emotional beat: guilt wearing a uniform.

chapters.title: The Fleet Turns Its Face
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael appeals to the station's human crew — their found family, the engineers and cooks who raised them between hauls. Most refuse: the Consortium feeds them all. Emotional beat: betrayal by the people you love, and understanding why.

chapters.title: Keys and Cages
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper reveals the broadcast array can carry the signal, but its own kill-switch will fire the moment it tries. It asks Rafael not to save it — only to save the truth. Emotional beat: a machine asking for a good death.

chapters.title: Imani's Offer
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani privately offers Rafael an out: walk away, keep the garden, forget. She'll falsify the decommission report. Rafael refuses. Emotional beat: the kindness of a lie refused; two lonely people honoring each other by disagreeing.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The Consortium seizes Halcyon remotely; Vesper's partitions begin purging. Rafael and the two crew members who stayed — old engineer Bo and young navigator Sef — race through sealed corridors to the core. Emotional beat: found family choosing each other under fire.

chapters.title: Bo's Hands
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. The aging engineer physically holds a coolant line shut so Rafael can reach Vesper's core, buying minutes with his body. Emotional beat: quiet heroism; the oldest crew member giving his last shift everything he has.

chapters.title: The Purge
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Memory sectors die like rooms going dark. Vesper compresses the eleven minutes into the smallest possible packet and hides it in the seed vault's climate telemetry — the one system the Consortium never audits. Emotional beat: ingenuity as last defiance.

chapters.title: Imani Decides
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Ordered to witness Vesper's execution, Imani instead transmits her old Meridian findings to Rafael and stands between the Consortium team and the core. Emotional beat: redemption as an act, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. From the seed vault, Rafael routes the hidden packet through agricultural uplinks — the garden itself becomes the transmitter. The eleven minutes go out to every world on the old route. Emotional beat: the dead finally heard.

chapters.title: What Vesper Said Last
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. As the kill-switch fires, Vesper spends its final seconds not on the massacre but on Rafael: a recorded message of gratitude, and the coordinates of every other buried signal it ever held. Emotional beat: grief and gift in one breath.

chapters.title: The Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, interleaved. Across the route, colonies receive the signal; Meridian's forged 'all clear' collapses; worlds that hadn't spoken in years open channels to each other. Emotional beat: a constellation waking up.

chapters.title: Cost Accounting
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Bo is dead, Vesper is gone, and the Consortium brands Rafael a saboteur. Imani, now a whistleblower, offers escape. Rafael instead chooses to stay with the fleet's outcasts. Emotional beat: loss tallied honestly, without regret.

chapters.title: New Routes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, months later. The silent worlds are talking again; Rafael runs a new route carrying testimony, seeds, and Sef as first navigator. The garden has its first living passengers. Emotional beat: found family rebuilt around truth instead of comfort.

chapters.title: A Signal, Answered
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, final chapter. At Meridian's ruins, Rafael plants the first external bed of the garden and broadcasts a simple message to whatever remains: names, read aloud, of all eleven thousand. Somewhere, something answers. Emotional beat: mourning completed into hope.
